explanations.explanation: Paran it is, baker! The text says Israel traveled "…from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran." (Numbers 10:12) That's a whole string of stops before the cloud finally stays put. I've been moved around a lot in my life, and I still wouldn't know when to unpack.

Zin is a good guess, friend, but it's not the one in this verse. Numbers 10:12 says the cloud settled "…in the Wilderness of Paran." Israel traveled from place to place before the cloud settled there. I'd have guessed wrong too, and I can't even work a map.

Shur is a decent guess, friend, but the verse points somewhere else. Numbers 10:12 says the cloud settled "…in the Wilderness of Paran." Israel goes from place to place first, and then the cloud settles. Nobody in that camp gets to say "are we there yet" and be right.

Ooh, not quite, friend. Picture a group chat where every leader votes on the departure time. That's not what happened here. The text says Israel set out "…according to the LORD’s command through Moses." (Numbers 10:13) The command came from the LORD, and the tribe leaders just got the memo. I bet they packed fast.
Right, friend. The text says they set out "…according to the LORD’s command through Moses." (Numbers 10:13) So the tribe leaders didn't decide it. The LORD gave the command, and Israel followed.

explanations.answer: The LORD has promised good things to Israel
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Moses says, "…for the LORD has promised good things to Israel." (Numbers 10:29) He's inviting Hobab to a promise, not just a trip. And he says they'll treat Hobab well.

explanations.answer: The LORD has given Israel a strong army
explanations.explanation: An army? Friend, that's a whole different invitation. Moses never brings one up. He says, "…for the LORD has promised good things to Israel." (Numbers 10:29) His pitch is a promise, plus "…we will treat you well…" Not a word about troops.

explanations.answer: The LORD has asked for Hobab by name
explanations.explanation: Moses never says the LORD asked for Hobab by name. He says, "…for the LORD has promised good things to Israel." (Numbers 10:29) That's the reason on the table. It's Moses doing the inviting here.

explanations.answer: Go back to his own land and people
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Hobab says, "I will not go… Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people." (Numbers 10:30) That's a clear answer. I think he's got home on his mind.

explanations.answer: Go on ahead to scout the way
explanations.explanation: Hobab doesn't offer to scout anything. He says, "I will not go… Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people." (Numbers 10:30) It's a plain no to Moses, and he says where he's headed instead.
Hobab doesn't say he'll hang around the mountain. He says, "I will not go… Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people." (Numbers 10:30) He's heading home, not staying put.

explanations.answer: Where they should camp in the wilderness
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moses says Hobab knows "…where we should camp in the wilderness…" and that he can "…serve as our eyes." (Numbers 10:31) Moses is asking Hobab to be Israel's eyes out there. It's a real need he's pointing to.

explanations.answer: How to speak with the kings nearby
explanations.explanation: Kings and diplomacy? Nope, Moses isn't asking Hobab to be a talker. He says, "…you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can serve as our eyes." (Numbers 10:31) The skill on the table is knowing where to camp. Hobab is wanted for his eyes, not his small talk.

explanations.answer: Which roads the enemy armies travel
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't mention roads or enemy armies. He says Hobab knows "…where we should camp in the wilderness…" so he can "…serve as our eyes." (Numbers 10:31) The need is about where to camp.
Yes, friend. Moses says, "…we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us." (Numbers 10:32) He doesn't offer Hobab a wage or a trade deal. He offers a share in whatever the LORD gives.

Trade is a fair guess, but Moses doesn't say it. He says, "…we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us." (Numbers 10:32) Sharing is a different thing than swapping. He's offering Hobab a part of the good things.

Store makes sense if you're picturing a pantry, but that's not the word. Moses says, "…we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us." (Numbers 10:32) He's promising to share, not to store anything up.

That's right, baker! The text says "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" was "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) The ark goes out in front, and Israel sets out from the mountain of the LORD behind it. Three days of that.

Moses is in this story, but he's not who the verse puts out in front. It says "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" was "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) No staff gets mentioned in this passage. The ark is the one named as going ahead.

The golden lampstand is a lovely piece, but it doesn't show up in this passage. What does show up is "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) I'd love a lampstand out front too, but the text names the ark. Next time, go with the ark.
You got it, baker. The ark goes ahead "…to seek a resting place for them." (Numbers 10:33) After three days of walking, a resting place sounds mighty good. The ark is out there looking for one.

A meeting place sounds sensible, friend, but that's not the word in the verse. The ark goes ahead "…to seek a resting place for them." (Numbers 10:33) The word is resting. Think of a long trip and ask yourself what you'd want at the end of it.

Hiding is a creative pick, but it's not the word here. The verse says the ark goes ahead "…to seek a resting place for them." (Numbers 10:33) Resting is what the ark is looking for. After three days on the road, I'd be looking for the same thing, and probably a chair.

True, friend. The text says, "…the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp." (Numbers 10:34) So the ark goes ahead, and the cloud is overhead. Israel isn't setting out without either one.
Not this time, friend. The text says, "…the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp." (Numbers 10:34) So the statement is true. The cloud is overhead as they leave.

explanations.answer: For the LORD to rise up and scatter His enemies
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moses says, "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." (Numbers 10:35) He says it every time the ark sets out. It's a prayer, spoken out loud.

explanations.answer: For the LORD to make the road ahead smooth
explanations.explanation: A smooth road would be nice after three days of walking, but Moses doesn't ask for it. He says, "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." (Numbers 10:35) He's asking about the LORD's enemies.

explanations.answer: For the LORD to send water to the camp
explanations.explanation: Water is a smart thing to want after three days of walking, friend. I'd have asked for it too, and for a chair. But that's not Moses' prayer. Whenever the ark sets out, he says, "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." (Numbers 10:35) His words are about the LORD's enemies being scattered, not about supplies.
